claims: Public grants should prioritise low-income households.
Insulation upgrades should be required before every heat pump installation.
Councils should coordinate street-by-street retrofit programmes.
Tenants should be protected from rent increases attributable to publicly funded upgrades.

panel.round1: Public funding should prioritise low-income households in the least efficient homes. Assess insulation and ventilation before specifying heating, but do not require every possible insulation measure before a heat pump. Councils should coordinate street-by-street upgrades where properties are similar, with independent quality checks. Protect tenants from rent increases caused by publicly funded works. Technical suitability matters more than a universal technology sequence.

Low-income households should receive grants first. I oppose a rule requiring insulation upgrades before every heat pump: suitable homes could decarbonise sooner. Street-by-street coordination is useful but households should retain a choice of installer. I support safeguards preventing grant-funded work from displacing tenants. Training and clear performance standards would matter more than another complicated eligibility test.
